answer: Treat a new identity as a climb, not a soft landing. Before it can mine or grade, the applicant must lock a stake on a scarce public ridge and keep it there through two quiet epochs, bound to a unique work signature and a path fingerprint. Overnight velvet onboarding is refused: a key with no delayed capital gets no seat. Graders watch for a ripple of near-identical answers or fingerprints arriving in lockstep. When that ripple forms, every unvested stake in the cluster is slashed and those ridge slots stay closed for a season, so farms buy delayed height instead of a velvet stack of names.
